title: Invertibility of the specified section-pullback tensor mate
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $X,Y$ be schemes in universe $u$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism. Use the fixed small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with objects and module sections in universe $u+1$ and morphisms in universe $u$. Write $R_T$ for the section-ring sheaf of the pulled-back coefficients on $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use exactly the coefficient map $c:R_Y\to f_*R_X$, section-module functors $L=f^*_{\rm sec}$ and $P=f_{*,\rm sec}$ and specified adjunction $L\dashv P$ of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Module tensors are the sheafified balanced tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and their units are the regular modules $R_T$. Let $P$ carry its uniquely normalized lax structure: its tensor maps send every local pure tensor over $V$ to the same pure tensor over $V\times_YX$, and its regular-unit map is $c$. Let $L$ have the oplax structure obtained as mate under the specified adjunction [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate], and write $a_M:M\to PLM$ for the adjunction unit. For all $R_Y$-module sheaves $M,N$, the tensor mate $\delta_{M,N}:L(M\otimes_{R_Y}N)\to LM\otimes_{R_X}LN$, defined as the adjunct of $M\otimes_{R_Y}N\xrightarrow{a_M\otimes a_N}PLM\otimes_{R_Y}PLN\xrightarrow{\mu_{LM,LN}}P(LM\otimes_{R_X}LN)$, is an isomorphism. This is invertibility of the actual chosen mate, with no flatness, finiteness, or boundedness hypothesis on $M,N$ or $f$.

proof.text: Use the existing internal pullback and its specified adjunction. Its normalized direct-image pairing agrees with the right-adjoint lax structure of the existing strong internal pullback: the balancing-projection equation determines the tensorator on pure tensors, and hence the entire lax structure. Thus internalPull_delta_isIso gives invertibility of the actual internal mate, with no additional assumptions. These are earlier proved declarations of the same module, based on [lem-sfb-trace-base-change-first] and [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate].

proof.text: Take the concrete tensor isomorphisms of the fixed internal-section equivalences from [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. They send internal pure tensors to section pure tensors and are natural in both variables. The direct-image comparison from [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] fixes every section. The internal pairing normalization and the section normalization [lem-pd-section-push-normalized-exists-unique] therefore make the tensor-pairing square commute on every pure tensor. Internal tensor hom extensionality extends this equality to the sheaf-module maps. The aliases and coefficient map remain exactly those of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data].

proof.text: The operations transport theorem gives the unit equation E(a_M);beta_LM;P(gamma_M)=b_EM for the specified adjunctions. First derive transport of the Hom bijections by expanding an adjunct as unit followed by direct image and using naturality of beta. Apply this to the internal tensor mate. The pairing square of Step 2, tensor naturality of E, and naturality of the section pairing identify its adjunct with the adjunct of gamma_(M tensor N);Lsec(e_MN);deltaSec_(EM,EN). Injectivity gives F(deltaInternal_MN);g_(LM,LN);(gamma_M tensor gamma_N)=gamma_(M tensor N);Lsec(e_MN);deltaSec_(EM,EN). All left-hand factors and the first two right-hand factors are isomorphisms, so the actual section mate is an isomorphism at EM,EN. This calculation is the private pullTensor_mate_transport helper, using the Mathlib mate formula [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate].

proof.text: For arbitrary section modules M,N take essential-preimage isomorphisms E(M0) to M and E(N0) to N supplied by the equivalence. Naturality of the actual oplax tensor map identifies its composite with the image of their tensor with the invertible tensor map of Step 3 followed by the tensor of their images. Cancel the invertible first factor to conclude IsIso(deltaSec_MN). All constructions work for the identity map, zero modules, zero coefficient ring, and empty sites; no flatness or boundedness hypothesis is introduced.
